newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spaniard held in Miami for breaking Cuba embargo.
newsitem.headline: Spaniard held in Miami for breaking Cuba embargo.

text.p: A Spanish businessman has been detained by U.S. customs in Miami on charges he violated a 1963 trade embargo against Cuba, Spanish officials said on Saturday.

Javier Ferreiro, who is from the northern Spanish port city La Coruna and a resident of Havana, was detained on April 1 for illegally exporting American goods worth some $350,000 to Cuba via the Dominican Republic.

A spokesman for the Spanish foreign ministry said the consulate in Miami was giving Ferreiro, 46, legal help and advice. He has appeared before a U.S. judge and is being held in a Miami, Florida, detention centre.
Spanish diplomatic sources in Washington said Ferreiro was accused of violating the 1963 law banning trade with Cuba and not the Helms-Burton law passed last year by Congress.
The Spanish foreign ministry said Spain opposed the U.S. embargo, but recognised it as a legitimate U.S. law.
Ferreiro, who operates his business out of Cuba in the hospitality sector, faces 10 to 16 months prison if convicted.
